status: planned; no new timing measurement or optimization claim
objective: Revisit the retained 11.5% updated hot-query observation against its actual historical baseline, preserving correctness and separating current aggregate changes from the prior allocation-only comparison.
method: Reuse the preserved deterministic retrieval-tail-20261031 probe and its exhaustive ordered-result oracle. Change only the required API compatibility, explicit source revision selection and evidence recording.
Build each pinned revision with Rust 1.99.0, identical optimization settings and counting allocator; record exact injected source and executable hashes.
Normalize old/new execute_search return types outside source under test; retain production Result checks in the current timed path.
Compare complete ordered result payloads across revisions and rounds outside timed regions; do not rely only on CRC fingerprints.
Rotate the three variant execution orders over five rounds, including reversed orders; use one Rust process at a time after all unrelated local builds/tests terminate.
Record host processes/load, filesystem, toolchain and per-round samples. Preserve all failed attempts and reject stale executables.
Report round-level paired p50/p95/p99 ratios and allocation counts; the 128-sample empirical p99 is not a population-tail estimate. Do not pool queries as independent process rounds.
acceptance: Every per-query exhaustive comparison and complete cross-revision ordered-result comparison must match.
Any sustained current hot-query median/empirical-p99 increase above 5% requires diagnosis before calling this local regression resolved.
Retain all observations even if noisy or unfavorable; no retries chosen to manufacture a faster result.
Only evidence-backed optimizations may follow; no change to correctness, limits, durability or deadlines for timing gains.
premeasurement_corrections: Reuse the System delegation pattern from benches/query_alloc.rs and benches/ingest_alloc.rs for alloc_zeroed and realloc. The inherited historical probe instead used GlobalAlloc's default allocate-copy-free realloc. Count successful allocation operations and requested live-byte deltas; allocator-internal transient storage and RSS remain unmeasured. Apply this corrected instrumentation identically to all three fresh variants; original measurements stay unchanged and are not directly comparable.

Bind builds and execution to plan, source, probe, harness and executable hashes; summarization rejects altered manifests or reports. Reject inherited WARM_PROBE_DISABLE_DELTA rather than silently changing maintenance.

Use a private target directory under this worktree for all benchmark variants; global Cargo configuration points to a shared build directory. The identical compiler, optimization, allocator and workload remain unchanged.

Historical/prior builds retain the complete build-time plan and hash. Before the first measurement their only permitted plan difference is the current comparison revision, allowing the fixed baselines to build while integration completes. Current-source builds require the exact final plan; all variants retain unchanged workload, harness, probe, compiler/settings and pinned source hashes.
limits: Local free synthetic development only; no paid APIs/cloud, models or model downloads.
The current revision contains many functional repairs; this comparison cannot causally attribute an aggregate timing change to one patch.
This is not a competitor benchmark, high-dimensional evaluation, hardware power-loss test, production latency guarantee or best-in-class claim.
Original October 29/31 measurements and their limits remain unchanged.

Complete result payloads are retained outside timed regions identically in each variant; this changes allocator history relative to the original harness. Compare new runs with each other, not directly with old absolute timing samples.
sustained_regression_rule: Median current round quantile exceeds the baseline median by over 5%, and at least four of the five paired rounds are slower; descriptive investigation trigger, not statistical significance.
